newsitem.title: PERU: Peru posts 2.2 pct Jan-Nov '96 cumulative GDP.
newsitem.headline: Peru posts 2.2 pct Jan-Nov '96 cumulative GDP.

text.p: The Peruvian economy grew 2.2 percent in the first 11 months of 1996, compared to 7.7 percent in the same period of 1995, the National Institute of Statistics and Information (INEI) said Saturday.
The INEI added that year-on-year Gross Domestic Product (GDP) rose 5.3 percent in November 1996, compared with 0.8 percent year-on-year growth in the same month in 1995.
The government is predicting annual growth of 2.5 percent in 1996, down from initial projections of between five and six percent due to a longer-than-expected economic slowdown.
It is aiming for five percent growth in 1997.
In 1995, the economy expanded 7.0 percent, Latin America's second-highest growth rate, down from 13.1 percent in 1994, according to revised Central Reserve Bank figures.

The central bank has said it often publishes GDP figures that differ slightly from those of the INEI because the bank -- issuing its figures up to weeks later -- collects its data from a wider ranger of sources. --Saul Hudson, Lima newsroom, 221-2134
